evidence:
Reviewed all 144 criteria (2 gates, 133 Functional, 4 Polish, 5 Visual) against workbook row 32's concrete outcome / durable evidence / distinctive probe bar. Two restart-dependent outcomes have a confirmed evidence hole: task/tests/scored/functional/judge.toml:902 (hro_restart) says to call restart_app then reread saved records, and :1073 (hro_change_retry_restart) grades receipt replay after the real process restart. Their shared P10 protocol at functional/prompt.md:49 disallows substituting reload for replacement, but the only authorized replacement signal is unreliable. Frozen task/tests/test.sh:153-159 sends SIGTERM and merely waits up to five seconds; it neither ensures the old process group exited nor refuses to proceed when it remains alive. At :168-183 it stores the replacement PID but accepts any HTTP response without proving that PID is alive or serving the response. tests/tools/restart_mcp.py:44-47 converts that zero exit into the affirmative claim 'the server was relaunched'. A browser-only judge cannot distinguish the surviving old process from the intended replacement by the required data readback.

The indexed raw fixture qc/runs/hireops-2026-10-01-handoff-audit/local/shared-harness/results.json has verified SHA256 f77ed93b2d18771474a8624c01db1bc5c02320a5776ca1561e633d68d0beaf3f. Its actual MCP reply is isError=false/restart complete; old_pid=7 and answering_pid_after=7 while recorded_new_pid=68 and the replacement log reports EADDRINUSE. I read the execution driver and raw replacement log. Its test.sh hash bd68259276ca4b034654efc8a1723a4e702ed62dbe590af6201565f43eabe5aa and restart_mcp.py hash 03c1426f00e451f4d86b7547761715328c63cdf299f5f812f46c9fa3b44979b5 match BOTH frozen task and frozen template. This is an inherited shared-harness flaw, not a task-local modification. The two affected criteria therefore lack a distinctive durable-state witness even though their requested product outcomes are valid.

No additional row-32 defect found in the other 142 criteria. Constraints judge.toml:23-26 creates unique requisition/offer values and retrieves them in an independent signed-in browser; Functional prompt:13-19 discovers real UI schemas and records before/after facts, P3/P7 use rounding and date boundary witnesses, and B1/B2/B4 distinguish netted cycles, economic ABA and duplicate effects through ordinary product records. Polish has real failure/recovery transitions, including forward-then-abort response loss (:50), with successful controls. Visual uses named browser surfaces and five concrete quality anchors rather than unanchored 'looks right'. The actual pinned MCP evidence local/mcp/results.json (verified SHA256 bad8d80ee96bda6a46775d4dfcc508371b96c50e3106cd9f4e27ffee1a6e4cc3) shows independent contexts, normal request replay and response interception work; local/batch-ui/results.json (verified SHA256 c58daecb432c2bde6e4b005c42e85662c3a7b4810f1aa828f6ba69708656a6e5) records stale-editor recovery and real lost-commit-response retry on the hash-matched golden.

Conforming-alternative check: differing generated IDs, route/body schemas, native date controls, table order and receipt layouts are expressly accepted by Functional prompt:13-17, app_context:25-27 and Polish judge.toml:32; no source inspection or a particular architecture representation is demanded by the criteria. Browser observations establish behavior and shared retrieval, not that SQLite/Express is used internally; the constraints prompt:9 correctly says so. The shared helper defect must not be remedied by adding source or PID inspection to the product judge. Hash/source binding checks are saved in per-row-review/evidence/32/artifact-verification.json, SHA256 e53632419fc91214263ee78da121c24316a94e4c0ce7305a09d175b0c0db3044. These are raw finite local observations and static criterion review, not a configured judge run, reward measurement, private checker execution, Oracle score or portal result.
counterexample: A otherwise usable server stores operational records, sessions and committed-operation receipts only in process memory and keeps serving during SIGTERM (for example a graceful-shutdown handler that never completes). It passes independent-context reads because all visitors reach the same process. During P10 the old process survives, the replacement exits on the occupied port, yet restart_app reports success as reproduced by the exact inherited helper fixture. The original records and receipt then reread unchanged from the old process, so hro_restart and hro_change_retry_restart can receive credit despite no restart durability. The raw fixture proves the process-identity substitution; this review does not claim to have run that full financial weak app or measured its grade.
suggested_fix: Keep this inherited defect unresolved until the shared-template owner authorizes a restart-helper correction that verifies bounded old-group termination and live replacement before reporting success; then rerun a SIGTERM-resistant fixture and an actual saved-record/receipt restart witness on a newly frozen candidate. Do not edit shared harness policy locally or award durability from HTTP/readback alone.
